text:
anna_ml: seeing divergence when running crimson-7b int8 with very long prefixes (~66k+). outputs match fp16 until a boundary then sudden token drift. quick repro and logs below.

anna_ml: repro steps:
```
1) load crimson-7b int8 (packed qkv)
2) feed ~66k token prefix (wiki-derived)
3) continue generation with a short prompt
4) diff logits vs fp16 baseline
```

anna_ml: symptoms: identical tokens up to ~65536 then repeated hallucination patterns and token repetition.

ben_runtime: paste the tiny log around the flip? i suspect a stride/alignment bug between dequant and kv write.

anna_ml: log excerpt (trimmed):
```
[2026-03-18T14:02:11Z] kv_cache_write idx=8191 len=64 src_off=524032 dst_off=524040
[2026-03-18T14:02:11Z] dequantize_block idx=8191 qstride=64 out_off=524032
[2026-03-18T14:02:11Z] kv_cache_write idx=8192 len=64 src_off=524096 dst_off=524104
[2026-03-18T14:02:11Z] dequantize_block idx=8192 qstride=64 out_off=524096
```
note dst_off frequently +8 relative to out_off.

carla_quant: +8 smells like an 8-byte padding/alignment slip. did we enable the memcpy fast-path in dequant recently? reinterpret/memcpy optimizations can bite on packed layouts.

anna_ml: yes, merged memcpy fast-path from PR #4021 (03/10). only fails on the int8 build; fp16 baseline clean.

ben_runtime: checklist: element size vs cache layout, allocator alignment vs qblock size, vectorized store tail handling. also check pinned page padding on certain dedicated nodes.

anna_ml: added assert in dequant kernel, failure trace:
```
ASSERT(ptr_offset % 8 == 0) failed at dequant.cu:142
ptr_offset=524040 expected=524032
```
so we hit an unexpected +8 offset.

carla_quant: can you try toggling USE_MEMCPY_DEQUANT=0 and re-run longctx? if memcpy is the culprit that should avoid the slip.

anna_ml: ran with USE_MEMCPY_DEQUANT=0 -> no divergence after 1k continuation tokens. seems to mitigate.

ben_runtime: that narrows it to the memcpy path. probable root: memcpy copies contiguous qblocks including padding bytes into consecutive cache slots; when prefix length % qblock != 0 the destination pointer math can shift by padding and accumulate at block boundaries.

carla_quant: i'll open a revert and add unit tests for boundary-crossing prefix lengths and fuzz +8/+16 alignment offsets.

dave_sre: note we should record which infra hit this. some dedicated nodes have different pinned allocator insertion padding which can cause small pointer deltas. capture node metadata.

anna_ml: saving failing seed/checkpoints to /mnt/artifacts/kv-padding/crimson-7b/seed-195/ and logs to /mnt/artifacts/logs/kv-pad-195.log. queued long-run eval overnight for 100k token compare.

carla_quant: PR #4089 opened to revert memcpy fastpath and add tests. perf impact: memcpy rollback costs ~6% token throughput in microbench; i think temporary rollback is fine. will rework fastpath to respect qblock stride/padding. assigning @ben_runtime for review.

deploy-bot: canary: staging/crimson-7b-int8 @carla_quant reverted memcpy-fastpath (PR #4089) deployed 2026-03-19T03:12:05Z

ben_runtime: after revert, add a lightweight runtime guard: if ptr_offset % 8 != 0 then fail early with clear error instead of silently corrupting KV. also add CI job: quantized longctx smoke at lengths 64k/65k/70k on PRs touching dequant/memcpy.

carla_quant: will add CI checks + perf regression test to track the ~6% delta. plan: implement memcpy respecting qblock stride (avoid copying padding into next slot) and reintroduce optimized path once validated.

anna_ml: thanks all. i'll report full eval numbers tomorrow. ping here if you see similar across other models.

ben_runtime: noted, thanks :thumbsup:
